note: Reproduced exactly from the daily closes. 234 sessions follow 5 or more closes in a row above the close before (the run counted up to the previous session); 116 of them closed above the previous close (49.6%). On any day: 3,524 of 6,665 = 52.9%. The 43.2%-55.9% range is the 95% Wilson interval for 116 of 234.

The day count agrees: 342 sessions follow a session that fell 2% or more, and 341 of them have 5 later sessions to measure. The move does not match the reading, which says it is measured 'from that session's close to the close 5 sessions later'. From the close of the session after the fall to the close 5 sessions later I get +0.62% on average (median +0.63%, higher on 58.7%, middle half -1.70% to +2.91%); if 'that session' is the one that fell, +0.79% (median +0.69%, higher on 59.5%). Strata's +0.85% / +0.78% / 60.1%, its quartiles (-1.73%, +3.38%) and its favourable/adverse medians (+2.71%, -2.54%) are all reproduced exactly when the move runs from the OPEN of the session after the fall to the close 5 sessions after that session, as the headline's 'from the open' says. So the arithmetic is sound, but the start point calculated (the open) is not the one the reading states (the close), and the window then spans 6 sessions rather than 5 (open to the close of the 5th session would be +0.72%, higher on 56.9%). The 'likely range' of the average (+0.36% to +1.33%) is consistent with a bootstrap of the open-based mean (mine, 10,000 resamples: bias-corrected +0.35% to +1.33%, plain percentile +0.35% to +1.33%; normal approximation +0.35% to +1.34%); its method is not stated and resampling is random, so it cannot be matched to the last digit.

Reproduced from the one-minute bars: 2,741 whole sessions from 2016-01-04 to 2026-11-27 (2019-08-12 is left out because its bars stop at 15:30). The session's low was first made between 09:30 and 10:00 on 926 sessions (33.8%) and between 15:30 and 16:00 on 361 (13.2%), the two largest shares; one part in 13 is 7.7%. Where the same low price occurs in more than one bar the first is taken; taking the last would give 33.6% and 13.4%. The 22 early-close sessions are included although they have no afternoon parts.

The day count agrees exactly (2,719 = the 2,741 whole minute-bar sessions less the 22 early closes, which have no 14:30 price; the 14:30 price is the close of the 14:29 bar and the close is the daily record's). The '0 days it happened (0.0%)' cannot be reproduced: no reading is shown and the summary describes a movement (the return from 14:30 to the close), which is a size, not an event that happens or does not. Measured as the summary describes, SPY moved +0.003% on average (median +0.013%), ending higher on 1,423 of 2,719 days (52.3%), lower on 1,295 and unchanged on 1. The largest rise was +5.34% (2020-03-13) and the largest fall -3.35% (2022-11-02), so 0 could be a true count only for a move beyond those, and nothing shown states such an event. The headline is therefore not a real count; it looks like a movement question answered through the 'how often' output with no event defined.

No reading is shown and the summary says only 'touch +1% from the open, open to close'. By that definition QQQ traded 1% or more above its open on 2,137 of 6,973 days (30.6%, interval 29.6%-31.7%), not 1,202, and with a single level there is no order of events to be unsure about. Best explanation: Strata's three counts are reproduced exactly by a rule with a second level that is stated nowhere in what I was given - 'reaches +1% above the open before -0.5% below it, by the close': happened 1,202 (696 daily-bar days plus 506 minute-bar days), did not 4,991, both levels inside one daily bar 780. Even under that rule the headline is inconsistent: 1,202 of 6,973 is 17.2%; the 19.4% (and the 18.4%-20.4% interval) is 1,202 of the 6,193 decided days. Convention concern: leaving the 780 undecidable days out is not neutral - every one of them did reach +1% - so the rate over all days lies somewhere between 17.2% and 28.4% (in the minute-bar years, where the order is known, +1% came first on 61 of the 216 sessions that touched both levels).

The 12:00 condition was not applied. SPY was below its open at 12:00 (close of the 11:59 bar below the 09:30 bar's open) on 1,254 of the 2,741 whole sessions, and closed above its open on 321 of those = 25.6% (interval 23.3%-28.1%). (Strata's 'days it didn't' of 1,254 is 2,741 minus 1,487; that it equals the number of sessions below the open at 12:00 is a coincidence.)

By the convention stated for the previous session's high, applied here to the low (the session's lows against the previous session's low from the daily record), SPY traded below the previous session's low on 3,824 of 8,515 days (44.9%, interval 43.9%-46.0%); the count is the same whether the session's low comes from the one-minute bars (2016 on) or the daily record. Counting a low equal to the previous low as well gives 3,875 (daily lows) or 3,871 (minute lows from 2016), 45.5%. Strata's 3,881 (45.6%) is reproduced exactly only by counting 'at or below' AND taking the previous session's low from that session's one-minute bars (2016 on) instead of the daily record. So two things depart from what is stated: 'trades below' is counted as 'at or below' (51 sessions have a low exactly equal to the previous low), and the previous low is not the daily record's (the two sources differ by more than a cent on 128 sessions since 2016, e.g. 2022-10-04: daily-record low 366.57, minute-bar low 372.31). Strata's own independent check also disagreed (3,870); my nearest figure to that is 3,871. The answer sam/sh-21#1 counts the same phrase strictly and against the daily record (1,198 sessions since 2016), so the two answers use different rules for 'trades below the previous session's low'.
